title: Generic enumeration of contracted components on a finite etale cover
statement: Let $T$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $Z\to T$ and $W\to T$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] families whose geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are empty or pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Suppose every nonsmooth point of a geometric fibre of $Z/T$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is an ordinary node, with completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] $F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over the algebraically closed residue field $F$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $h:Z\to W$ be a proper $T$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Every reduced irreducible component of a geometric fibre of $Z/T$ that $h$ maps to one point is proper over that geometric residue field. There exist a nonempty affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum] open $U\subseteq T$, an integral affine scheme $S$ and a finite etale surjective morphism $\pi:S\to U$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and a finite list of closed subschemes $H_1,\ldots,H_n\hookrightarrow Z\times_T S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product], flat and finitely presented over $S$, with the following properties. For every geometric point $\bar s$ of $S$, the fibres $H_{i,\bar s}$ are precisely all the reduced irreducible components of $Z_{\bar s}$, each once [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a fixed subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $h_{\bar s}$ maps $H_{i,\bar s}$ to one point if and only if $i\in J$. Writing $\xi$ for the generic point of $S$ [def-sc-generic-point], each $H_{i,\xi}$ with $i\in J$ is proper over $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. No properness of $Z/T$, $W/T$ or $H_i/S$, and no generic-isomorphism or modification hypothesis, is assumed or concluded. The list and $J$ may be empty.

source.place: Tags 0551 (lemma-make-components-generic-fibre-geometrically-irreducible), 0559 (lemma-geom-irreducible-generic-fibre), and the closure argument of 055A (lemma-nr-geom-irreducible-components-good); combined agent-extracted refinement for a proper map of nodal curves with a fixed contracted sublist. The contracted-component locus is the one used in Temkin Lemma 5.1(ii), printed p. 34 (EGA IV3 13.1.3).

proof.text: First prove the assertion about a contracted component in an arbitrary geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field $F$. Let $R\hookrightarrow Z_F$ be that reduced component and suppose its image is $\{w\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], $h_F$ is proper and its composite with this closed immersion is proper. Its image is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence $w$ is a closed point of $W_F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], $\kappa(w)=F$. The map from the reduced scheme $R$ factors through this reduced point: on an affine neighbourhood of $w$, every element of its maximal ideal pulls back into every prime of each affine open of $R$, hence to zero. Thus $R$ is a closed subscheme of the proper fibre $h_F^{-1}(w)$. Properness under base change and composition, again [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], proves $R/F$ proper. This does not use properness of either ambient curve over $F$.

source.place: Properness from the definition, morphisms.tex Tag 01W1, base change and closed immersions; algebra.tex Tag 00FV for the closed image point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-etale-generic-component-splitting] to $Z\to T$, which is finite type because it is finitely presented. Obtain $U_0$, $S_0$ and $\pi_0:S_0\to U_0$. Write $K=\kappa(\xi)$ for the generic field of the integral affine $S_0$. The schemes $S_0,Z_{S_0},W_{S_0}$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Hence the generic fibre has finitely many components. Give their closures in $Z_{S_0}$ the reduced induced closed structures $H_i$ using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Their generic fibres are the reduced generic components $C_i$: on affine charts this is the equality between the radical ideal of a closure and the contraction of the generic radical ideal, followed by localization to $K$.

source.place: Tags 0551 and 055A, first reduction and the paragraph taking the closures of generic components.

proof.text: Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $T$, $k=\kappa(\eta)$, and $\bar k$ the algebraic closure fixed in [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. The finite map $\pi_0$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] and surjective onto the irreducible $U_0$, so $\pi_0(\overline{\{\xi\}})=\overline{\{\pi_0(\xi)\}}=U_0$ and $\pi_0(\xi)=\eta$; hence $k\subseteq K$ and $Z_K=Z_k\times_kK$. By hypothesis every nonsmooth point of the geometric generic fibre $Z_{\bar k}$ has completed local ring $\bar k[[u,v]]/(uv)$, so $Z_{\bar k}$ is reduced by [lem-trf-nodal-points-reduced-algebraically-closed], and $Z_k$ is geometrically reduced by [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test]. So is $Z_K$, since $(Z_K)_L=(Z_k)_L$ for every $L/K$. Only the fixed algebraic closure of the hypothesis is used; no nodal property over larger algebraically closed fields is claimed. Each reduced component $C_i$ is geometrically reduced as well. Here are the local details needed for [lem-pur-geometric-reducedness-from-generic-stalks]: at its generic point choose an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Z_K$ and its minimal prime $\mathfrak p$. Since $B$ is reduced, $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is a field and is also the generic local ring of $C_i$. For every extension $L/K$, $B_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_K L$ is a localization of the reduced ring $B\otimes_K L$, and is reduced (a nilpotent fraction has zero numerator after multiplication by a denominator). Thus the cited criterion applies to the reduced $C_i$. Together with the geometric irreducibility supplied in Step 2, $C_i$ is geometrically integral. No quotient by an arbitrary prime is being asserted geometrically reduced.

source.place: curves.tex Tag 0E37; varieties.tex Tags 04KS and 035W, applied only at the minimal primes of the reduced generic fibre.

proof.text: Every $H_i\to S_0$ is finite type. It is finitely presented: on affine charts apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], and use [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] for quasi-separatedness, together with its quasi-compactness. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flatness] to each $H_i/S_0$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-geometric-irreducibility-shrink] and [lem-trf-generic-constancy-geometric-reducedness] to each $H_i/S_0$ using Step 3. Intersect the finitely many resulting nonempty opens of $S_0$. Over this open all $H_i$ are flat and finitely presented, and all their geometric fibres are nonempty, reduced and irreducible. Empty index sets require no shrinking.

source.place: Tags 052A, 0559 and 0578; algebra.tex Tag 00FP and properties.tex Tag 01OY for the finite presentation hypotheses.

proof.text: Arrange that these fibres enumerate all components, with no repetitions. The complement $B=Z_{S_0}\setminus\bigcup_i|H_i|$ has empty generic fibre. It is finite type and finitely presented over the Noetherian $S_0$, so [lem-weil-pbc-chevalley-constructible-image] makes its image constructible. A constructible subset missing the generic point of an irreducible Noetherian scheme is not dense: write it as a finite union of locally closed subsets as in [def-weil-constructible-subset]; a dense such piece would contain a nonempty open, hence the generic point. Remove the closure of this image. The $H_i$ now cover every fibre topologically, also after field extension by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applied to their finite disjoint union. Further apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-component-lower-bound] to $Z_{S_0}/S_0$, whose ordinary generic fibre has exactly $n$ components. Each ordinary fibre has at least $n$ components and thus its geometric fibre has at least $n$: every ordinary component generic point has a lift after field extension, and a geometric irreducible component maps into only one ordinary component. But the geometric fibre is covered by $n$ nonempty irreducible closed sets $H_{i,\bar s}$, so has at most $n$ components. Therefore these sets are exactly its components, each once. Reducedness from Step 4 and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] give the required closed subschemes. If $n=0$, the complement argument makes $Z$ empty here.

source.place: Tag 055A, closure-cover and component lower-bound argument; Tags 054J and 0554; topology.tex Tag 005L.

proof.text: For each $i$ form the closed set $h(|H_i|)\subseteq W_{S_0}$, closed because $H_i\to W_{S_0}$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Let $Q_i$ be its reduced induced closed subscheme, from [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. There is a factorization $q_i:H_i\to Q_i$: locally every element of the radical ideal defining $Q_i$ pulls back into every prime of the reduced $H_i$, hence to zero. This factorization is surjective by its construction. It is proper: its base change along the closed immersion $Q_i\hookrightarrow W_{S_0}$ is $H_i\to W_{S_0}$ pulled back to $Q_i$, with source canonically $H_i$ since the defining ideal already acts by zero. Use proper base change in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] identifies the underlying set of $Q_{i,\bar s}$ with the image of $H_{i,\bar s}$ under $h_{\bar s}$ for every geometric point. In particular this image is nonempty and irreducible. This is a topological image assertion; it does not assume that formation of a scheme-theoretic image commutes with arbitrary base change.

source.place: Closed-image construction following Tag 055A; properness from morphisms.tex Tag 01W1 and surjective base change Tag 01S1.

proof.text: Each $Q_i/S_0$ is finite type, being a closed subscheme of the Noetherian finite type $W_{S_0}$. Its generic fibre is nonempty by the surjectivity in Step 6, and is a closed subset of the pure one-dimensional $W_K$, so $d_i=\dim Q_{i,\xi}$ is either $0$ or $1$. Apply [lem-trf-generic-fibre-dimension-neighborhood] to each $Q_i/S_0$ and shrink simultaneously so that all its ordinary fibres have dimension $d_i$. After any residue-field extension their dimensions are unchanged by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change]. Define $J=\{i\mid d_i=0\}$. For a geometric point, $Q_{i,\bar s}$ is nonempty and irreducible by Step 6. Such a zero-dimensional scheme has only one point: a distinct point specializing from its generic point would be a chain of two irreducible closed subsets. Conversely a singleton has dimension zero. Thus $h_{\bar s}$ contracts $H_{i,\bar s}$ exactly when $i\in J$. No properness of $Q_i/S_0$ is used.

source.place: Tag 05F7 (lemma-dimension-in-neighbourhood); morphisms.tex Tag 02FY for field extension of fibres.

proof.text: For $i\in J$, base change $H_{i,\xi}=C_i$ to an algebraic closure $\overline K$. Steps 5--7 show that it is a contracted reduced component of $Z_{\overline K}$. Step 1 makes it proper over $\overline K$. Apply [lem-pc-proper-descends-field] to the finite type $K$-scheme $C_i$ and the extension $\overline K/K$ to obtain properness of $H_{i,\xi}$ over $K$. This is only a statement about the generic fibre.

source.place: descent.tex Tag 02L1, properness descends under a field extension.

proof.text: Finally retain a finite etale cover of an open of the original base, rather than merely an open of the covering scheme. Let $V\subseteq S_0$ be the common open on which Steps 4--7 hold. Its complement is closed, and its image under the finite map $\pi_0$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. This image misses the generic point of $U_0$: the generic fibre of the integral finite cover $S_0/U_0$ is the spectrum of its fraction field and has the single point $\xi\in V$. Choose a nonempty principal affine open $U$ in the complementary open of $U_0$. Set $S=S_0\times_{U_0}U$ and restrict the $H_i$. This is an integral affine scheme (a nonzero principal localization of the domain of $S_0$); $S\to U$ remains finite etale by the definitions and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Moreover $S\subseteq V$. All conclusions established above therefore hold over $S$, with the same finite list, generic field and subset $J$.

source.place: Tag 0551, final closed-image shrinking; morphisms.tex Tags 01WN and 01S1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q25-8b59f6bc0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, the new node, every cited statement, Stacks 0551 (more-morphisms.tex, statement and proof) and 025O (etale.tex). The new node lem-trf-finite-etale-generic-component-splitting is correct: it is 0551 over an integral Noetherian base, and S is integral because A' is finite over Noetherian A and étale over reduced local rings, so 025O applies. It is not a duplicate (I ran rg for 0551 and the label, and read lem-sbc-generic-components-split and lem-trf-geometric-component-count-generic-constancy) and not a restated clause. Steps 1, 2 and 4-9 check out against their cited statements: proper image closed and residue field F; reduced closures; finite presentation, generic flatness, irreducibility shrink and reducedness constancy; Chevalley with the non-dense constructible argument and exact component count; closed image Q_i under base change; dimension-0 test; field descent of properness; principal open under the finite map. One fault (E1/C4), repaired: Step 3 applied lem-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres-reduced to Z_K.
